recipes.subject: the 4:3 recompose step survives and reproduces a 1440x1080 still from a real cast today
recipes.observed: Exit 0. stdout: '/tmp/probe43.png mode=tight window=62x20ch aspect=1.327 card_px_per_char=5.36'. PIL reports OUT (1440, 1080) ratio 1.3333333333333333 — exact 4:3. Also emits -card340.png (340x255) and -card240.png (240x180) for card-size judgement. agg render params fixed in epic9frames/crop.py: --theme asciinema --font-size 32 --idle-time-limit 0.05 --speed 50 --fps-cap 5 --last-frame-duration 2. Measured agg metrics hard-coded in compose43: char advance 19.3, line height 44.75, outer padding 17.5x/23.25y — derived from 100x30 vs 110x42 renders, so they are only valid for casts recorded at those terminal dims.

recipes.subject: recorded casts are 100x30, NOT the doctrine's --cols 80 --rows 24
recipes.observed: Header: {"version":3,"term":{"cols":100,"rows":30},"timestamp":1785504868,"idle_time_limit":2.0,"command":"bash .../media/driver.sh ..."}. The published jarl-media-doctrine paper states 'set --cols 80 --rows 24'. Every accepted 4:3 still on jarl.no was in fact composed from a 100x30 cast, and compose43's crop metrics were measured at 100x30. A new recording at 80x24 would silently break the hard-coded ADV/LH/PX/PY constants. The header also leaks the absolute scratchpad path in `command` — that is the header-scrub obligation.

recipes.subject: the upload wrapper survives, its admin token is still valid, and every asset it published is still live
recipes.observed: GET /v1/media/production -> 200, {"result":{"count":47,...}}. The published 4:3 recompose returns 200 / 182437 bytes.
